subject.title: Telegram: long tool-heavy turns give no activity feedback by default — silent partial mode reads as a dead bot

question: Should Telegram long-turn tool activity become visible by default, and should that happen through mode-independent quiet-work notes, a progress-mode default, or a session-level streaming command?
rationale: Current main already has opt-in progress plumbing and an open session-command PR, but changing defaults or adding independent status notes affects existing Telegram UX and channel behavior.

options.title: Add mode-independent quiet-work notes
options.body: Keep partial answer streaming as the default while adding a bounded, throttled status edit after a quiet active-tool interval, backed by live Telegram proof.

options.title: Make progress the Telegram default
options.body: Use the existing progress draft as the default Telegram experience, accepting a compatibility-sensitive change in visible edit cadence and chat behavior.

options.title: Land the session stream command first
options.body: Provide user self-service through the existing session-command work, while acknowledging it does not fully solve the default dead-bot perception for first-time users.

recommendation.title: Add mode-independent quiet-work notes
recommendation.body: Keep partial answer streaming as the default while adding a bounded, throttled status edit after a quiet active-tool interval, backed by live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored this report and have recent merged history across the exact Telegram progress and agent-progress surfaces.
